subproblems.title: Countable gluing of fibre-sum area identities over disjoint pieces and a null remainder
subproblems.statement: Let X, Y be measurable spaces, μ a measure on X, ν a measure on Y, f : X → Y, h, F : X → [0,∞], A, Z ⊆ X and B : ℕ → Set X such that (a) B_m ⊆ A for all m, (b) the B_m are pairwise disjoint, (c) every B_m is μ-null-measurable, (d) A ⊆ Z ∪ ⋃_m B_m, (e) μ(Z) = 0, (f) ν(f(Z)) = 0, and (g) for every m the fibre sum N_{B_m}(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B_m, f(x) = y} h(x) is ν-a.e. measurable and ∫_{B_m} F dμ = ∫_Y N_{B_m} dν. Then N_A(y) := Σ_{x ∈ A, f(x) = y} h(x) is ν-a.e. measurable and ∫_A F dμ = ∫_Y N_A dν.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (X Y : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace Y] (μ : Measure X) (ν : Measure Y) (f : X → Y) (h F : X → ℝ≥0∞) (A Z : Set X) (B : ℕ → Set X), (∀ m, B m ⊆ A) → Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint B) → (∀ m, NullMeasurableSet (B m) μ) → (A ⊆ Z ∪ ⋃ m, B m) → μ Z = 0 → ν (f '' Z) = 0 → (∀ m, AEMeasurable (fun y => ∑' x : {x : X // x ∈ B m ∧ f x = y}, h x) ν ∧ ∫⁻ x in B m, F x ∂μ = ∫⁻ y, ∑' x : {x : X // x ∈ B m ∧ f x = y}, h x ∂ν) → AEMeasurable (fun y => ∑' x : {x : X // x ∈ A ∧ f x = y}, h x) ν ∧ ∫⁻ x in A, F x ∂μ = ∫⁻ y, ∑' x : {x : X // x ∈ A ∧ f x = y}, h x ∂ν
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the summation device of steps 5, 6 and 7 of the parent proof (summing the area identities over the disjoint balls D_{j,m}, over the disjoint chart pieces A_j, and discarding the null part A_∞ whose f-image is null), isolated as one general measure-theoretic lemma. All sums are unordered sums in [0,∞] (∑' over subtypes), which may be regrouped arbitrarily.

1. (Fibre decomposition off f(Z).) Fix y ∉ f(Z). Then {x : x ∈ A ∧ f(x) = y} = ⋃_m {x : x ∈ B_m ∧ f(x) = y}, and the sets on the right are pairwise disjoint. Indeed, if x ∈ A and f(x) = y, then by (d) either x ∈ Z, which is impossible because then y = f(x) ∈ f(Z), or x ∈ B_m for some m. Conversely B_m ⊆ A by (a). Disjointness follows from (b).
2. (Sums over disjoint unions.) For pairwise disjoint sets S_m, the unordered [0,∞]-sum of h over ⋃_m S_m equals Σ_m of the sums over S_m: transport the sum along the equivalence ⋃_m S_m ≃ Σ_m S_m (Set.unionEqSigmaOfDisjoint; use Equiv.tsum_eq for its inverse, whose underlying point is the second component) and split the sum over the sigma type (ENNReal.tsum_sigma'). By step 1, N_A(y) = Σ_m N_{B_m}(y) for every y ∉ f(Z). (The subtype {x // x ∈ S ∧ f x = y} is definitionally the coercion of the set {x | x ∈ S ∧ f x = y}.)
3. (A.e. identity.) By (f), ν-a.e. y lies outside f(Z) (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem), so N_A = Σ_m N_{B_m} ν-a.e. No measurability of f(Z) is needed.
4. (Measurability, first conclusion.) Each N_{B_m} is ν-a.e. measurable by (g); a countable sum of a.e.-measurable [0,∞]-valued functions is a.e. measurable (AEMeasurable.ennreal_tsum, a deprecated alias that still compiles; or AEMeasurable.tsum); a function ν-a.e. equal to an a.e.-measurable function is a.e. measurable (AEMeasurable.congr with step 3). Hence N_A is ν-a.e. measurable.
5. (Target side.) ∫ N_A dν = ∫ Σ_m N_{B_m} dν (lintegral_congr_ae with step 3) = Σ_m ∫ N_{B_m} dν (lintegral_tsum, using the a.e.-measurability from (g)) = Σ_m ∫_{B_m} F dμ (by (g)).
6. (Source side.) A and ⋃_m B_m differ by a μ-null set: (⋃_m B_m) ∖ A = ∅ by (a), and A ∖ ⋃_m B_m ⊆ Z by (d), with μ(Z) = 0 by (e). Hence A =ᵐ[μ] ⋃_m B_m (ae_eq_set) and μ⌞A = μ⌞⋃_m B_m (Measure.restrict_congr_set). The B_m are μ-null-measurable by (c) and pairwise disjoint, hence pairwise a.e.-disjoint, so countable additivity of the set integral gives ∫_{⋃_m B_m} F dμ = Σ_m ∫_{B_m} F dμ for the arbitrary function F ≥ 0 (lintegral_iUnion₀; no measurability of F is required).
7. (Second conclusion.) By steps 5 and 6, ∫_A F dμ = Σ_m ∫_{B_m} F dμ = ∫_Y N_A dν. ∎
proof_key_steps: For y ∉ f(Z), the A-fibre over y is the disjoint union of the B_m-fibres (uses A ⊆ Z ∪ ⋃B_m and B_m ⊆ A).
Unordered [0,∞]-sums split over disjoint unions (unionEqSigmaOfDisjoint + ENNReal.tsum_sigma'), so N_A = Σ_m N_{B_m} off f(Z).
ν(f(Z)) = 0 gives N_A = Σ_m N_{B_m} ν-a.e.; AEMeasurable.ennreal_tsum + congr gives a.e.-measurability of N_A.
lintegral_tsum and the piecewise identities give ∫ N_A dν = Σ_m ∫_{B_m} F dμ.
A =ᵐ[μ] ⋃B_m (difference ⊆ Z), restrict_congr_set and lintegral_iUnion₀ give ∫_A F dμ = Σ_m ∫_{B_m} F dμ.

subproblems.title: Area formula with fibre-sum measurability for locally Lipschitz maps on open subsets of ℝⁿ
subproblems.statement: Let n, Q ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q locally Lipschitz on Ω, D ⊆ Ω Lⁿ-null-measurable, and w : ℝⁿ → [0,∞] a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞D. With Ju(x) := √det(⟨Du(x)e_i, Du(x)e_j⟩)_{i,j}, Du(x) = fderiv ℝ u x, the fibre sum N(y) := Σ_{x ∈ D, u(x) = y} w(x) is Hⁿ-a.e. measurable on ℝ^Q and ∫_D w(x)·Ju(x) dLⁿ(x) = ∫_{ℝ^Q} N dHⁿ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n Q : ℕ) (Ω D : Set (Eucl n)) (u : Eucl n → Eucl Q) (w : Eucl n → ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen Ω → LocallyLipschitzOn Ω u → D ⊆ Ω → NullMeasurableSet D (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) → AEMeasurable w ((volume : Measure (Eucl n)).restrict D) → AEMeasurable (fun y => ∑' x : {x : Eucl n // x ∈ D ∧ u x = y}, w x) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) ∧ ∫⁻ x in D, w x * ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ u x (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ u x (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det) ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl n)) = ∫⁻ y, ∑' x : {x : Eucl n // x ∈ D ∧ u x = y}, w x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure); Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i : Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ. For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, JT := √det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Gram-determinant Jacobian); for a map φ, Jφ(w) := J(fderiv ℝ φ w). For B ⊆ X, a map f and a weight h ≥ 0, the fibre sum is N_B(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B, f(x) = y} h(x), the unordered sum in [0,∞] (∑' over the subtype {x // x ∈ B ∧ f x = y}). c-antilipschitz on Ω means c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is step 5 of the parent proof (area formula for u_j = f∘Φ_j with measurability, via a countable cover by balls on which u_j is Lipschitz) for a general locally Lipschitz u; it is also the engine of step 4. Add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaDomain` to the Submission header (or to a new file under GMT/Ch06/ that the Submission imports); it transitively imports Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.NormDet, so LinearMap.normDet and Matrix.gram become available. Adding this import was checked to leave all Contract definitions and all frozen statement types unchanged (the comparator only byte-checks the Contract and Lake files). Do not re-prove the Euclidean area formula: use the SimonGMT theorems cited below.

1. (Jacobian normalization.) For every linear T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q, normDet(T) = JT. Indeed (e_i) is the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply: its i-th vector is EuclideanSpace.single i 1), so LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram gives normDet(T)² = det(Matrix.gram ℝ (T e_·)) = det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Matrix.gram is Matrix.of fun i j => ⟪v i, v j⟫); since normDet(T) ≥ 0 (LinearMap.normDet_nonneg), normDet(T) = √(normDet(T)²) = JT.
2. (Countable Lipschitz cover.) For each x ∈ Ω, local Lipschitzness gives K_x ≥ 0 and t_x ∈ 𝓝[Ω] x with u K_x-Lipschitz on t_x; as Ω is open, 𝓝[Ω] x = 𝓝 x (IsOpen.nhdsWithin_eq), so there is r_x > 0 with ball(x, r_x) ⊆ t_x ∩ Ω. These balls cover Ω and ℝⁿ is second countable, so a countable S ⊆ Ω satisfies Ω ⊆ ⋃_{x ∈ S} ball(x, r_x) (TopologicalSpace.countable_cover_nhdsWithin). If S = ∅ then Ω = ∅ and D = ∅: every fibre is empty, N ≡ 0 (measurable) and both integrals vanish. Otherwise write S = {s_0, s_1, …} (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range) and put V_m := ball(s_m, r_{s_m}): V_m is open, V_m ⊆ Ω, u is K_m-Lipschitz on V_m (K_m := K_{s_m}), and Ω ⊆ ⋃_m V_m.
3. (Disjoint pieces.) Let V′_m := V_m ∖ ⋃_{l<m} V_l (disjointed V): Borel, pairwise disjoint, V′_m ⊆ V_m and ⋃_m V′_m = ⋃_m V_m (iUnion_disjointed). Put D_m := D ∩ V′_m. Then D_m ⊆ D, D_m ⊆ V_m, the D_m are pairwise disjoint, each D_m is Lⁿ-null-measurable, and D ⊆ ⋃_m D_m because D ⊆ Ω ⊆ ⋃_m V′_m.
4. (Area formula on one piece.) Fix m. u is K_m-Lipschitz on D_m ⊆ V_m, D_m is null-measurable, and w is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞D_m (AEMeasurable.mono_set, D_m ⊆ D). The weighted area formula for Lipschitz maps on measurable subsets of ℝⁿ (Simon Ch. 2 (3.5); SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum with E = ℝⁿ, F = ℝ^Q, finrank ℝ ℝⁿ = n by finrank_euclideanSpace_fin) and its measurability companion (aemeasurable_weightedAreaFiberSum_lipschitzOn) state that N_m(y) := Σ_{x ∈ D_m, u(x) = y} w(x) (which is weightedAreaFiberSum D_m u w y by definition) is Hⁿ-a.e. measurable and ∫ N_m dHⁿ = ∫_{D_m} normDet(fderivWithin ℝ u D_m x)·w(x) dLⁿ(x) (the integrand is ENNReal.ofReal (areaJacobianWithin u D_m x) * w x).
5. (Within-derivative versus derivative.) Let g_m be a global Lipschitz extension of u|V_m (exists_lipschitz_extension_finiteDimensional), so u = g_m on V_m. By ae_fderivWithin_eq_of_lipschitz_extension (applied to D_m, with u = g_m on D_m), fderivWithin ℝ u D_m x = fderiv ℝ g_m x for Lⁿ⌞D_m-a.e. x. For x ∈ D_m ⊆ V_m, u and g_m agree on the open neighbourhood V_m of x, so fderiv ℝ u x = fderiv ℝ g_m x (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). Hence for Lⁿ⌞D_m-a.e. x, normDet(fderivWithin ℝ u D_m x) = normDet(fderiv ℝ u x) = Ju(x) by step 1, and therefore ∫_{D_m} w·Ju dLⁿ = ∫ N_m dHⁿ (lintegral_congr_ae and commutativity of multiplication).
6. (Gluing.) Apply the sibling lemma fiber_sum_glue with X = ℝⁿ, μ = Lⁿ, Y = ℝ^Q, ν = Hⁿ, map u, weight h := w, integrand F(x) := w(x)·ofReal(Ju(x)), A := D, Z := ∅ and B := (D_m)_m: (a)–(c) and (d) D ⊆ ∅ ∪ ⋃_m D_m hold by step 3, (e) Lⁿ(∅) = 0, (f) Hⁿ(u(∅)) = Hⁿ(∅) = 0, and (g) holds by steps 4–5. Its conclusions are exactly the two claims. ∎
proof_key_steps: normDet T = √det Gram(T e_i) (LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram with EuclideanSpace.basisFun).
Countable cover of Ω by balls V_m ⊆ Ω on which u is Lipschitz (countable_cover_nhdsWithin); empty case trivial.
Disjoint null-measurable pieces D_m = D ∩ disjointed V m covering D.
SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum and aemeasurable_weightedAreaFiberSum_lipschitzOn on each D_m.
fderivWithin u D_m = fderiv u a.e. on D_m via a Lipschitz extension (ae_fderivWithin_eq_of_lipschitz_extension, EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
Glue the pieces with fiber_sum_glue (Z = ∅).

subproblems.title: Antilipschitz charts pull back Hⁿ-null sets to Lⁿ-null sets
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ and c > 0 with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω. Then for every Z ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(Z) = 0 we have Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → (∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → ∀ Z : Set (Eucl P), (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) Z = 0 → (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' Z) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure); Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i : Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ. For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, JT := √det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Gram-determinant Jacobian); for a map φ, Jφ(w) := J(fderiv ℝ φ w). For B ⊆ X, a map f and a weight h ≥ 0, the fibre sum is N_B(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B, f(x) = y} h(x), the unordered sum in [0,∞] (∑' over the subtype {x // x ∈ B ∧ f x = y}). c-antilipschitz on Ω means c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is the estimate of step 1 of the parent proof: Ψ = (Φ|Ω)⁻¹ is (1/c)-Lipschitz, so it maps Hⁿ-null subsets of Φ(Ω) to Lⁿ-null sets (Lⁿ(Ψ(Z)) ≤ c^{−n} Hⁿ(Z)).

1. Φ is injective on Ω: if Φ(w) = Φ(w′) with w, w′ ∈ Ω then c|w − w′| ≤ 0, so |w − w′| = 0 since c > 0.
2. If Ω = ∅, then Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z) = ∅ and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise ℝⁿ is nonempty and Ψ := Function.invFunOn Φ Ω satisfies Ψ(Φ(w)) = w for all w ∈ Ω (Set.InjOn.leftInvOn_invFunOn).
3. Ψ is c⁻¹-Lipschitz on Φ(Ω): for y = Φ(w), y′ = Φ(w′) with w, w′ ∈ Ω, |Ψ(y) − Ψ(y′)| = |w − w′| ≤ c⁻¹|Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| = c⁻¹|y − y′| (LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul with constant Real.toNNReal c⁻¹).
4. Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z) ⊆ Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω)): if w ∈ Ω and Φ(w) ∈ Z then Φ(w) ∈ Z ∩ Φ(Ω) and Ψ(Φ(w)) = w.
5. Lipschitz maps increase Hⁿ by at most the n-th power of the constant (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, scaled by the normalizing factor of μHE[n]; packaged as SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, which is in scope): Hⁿ(Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω))) ≤ (c⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω)) ≤ (c⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(Z) = 0.
6. On ℝⁿ, Lⁿ = Hⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). By monotonicity and steps 4–5, Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = Hⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) ≤ Hⁿ(Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω))) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Antilipschitz with c > 0 gives injectivity on Ω; Ψ := invFunOn Φ Ω is a left inverse on Ω.
Ψ is c⁻¹-Lipschitz on Φ(Ω).
Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z) ⊆ Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω)).
Hⁿ Lipschitz image bound (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn) gives Hⁿ(Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω))) = 0.
Lⁿ = Hⁿ on ℝⁿ concludes.

subproblems.title: Change of variables through an injective Lipschitz–antilipschitz chart
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz on Ω and c-antilipschitz on Ω for some c > 0, A ⊆ Φ(Ω) Hⁿ-null-measurable, and g : ℝ^P → [0,∞] a.e.-measurable for Hⁿ⌞A. Let D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A) and JΦ(w) := √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩), DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w. Then D is Lⁿ-null-measurable, g∘Φ is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞D, and ∫_A g dHⁿ = ∫_D g(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dLⁿ(w).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (A : Set (Eucl P)) (g : Eucl P → ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen Ω → (∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith K Φ Ω) → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → A ⊆ Φ '' Ω → NullMeasurableSet A (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → AEMeasurable g ((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict A) → NullMeasurableSet (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A) (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) ∧ AEMeasurable (fun w => g (Φ w)) ((volume : Measure (Eucl n)).restrict (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A)) ∧ ∫⁻ x in A, g x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) = ∫⁻ w in Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A, g (Φ w) * ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det) ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl n))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure); Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i : Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ. For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, JT := √det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Gram-determinant Jacobian); for a map φ, Jφ(w) := J(fderiv ℝ φ w). For B ⊆ X, a map f and a weight h ≥ 0, the fibre sum is N_B(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B, f(x) = y} h(x), the unordered sum in [0,∞] (∑' over the subtype {x // x ∈ B ∧ f x = y}). c-antilipschitz on Ω means c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is step 4 of the parent proof (area formula for the injective Lipschitz chart Φ_j, transferring integrals over A_j to D_j, with the null-measurability of D_j and the a.e.-measurability of g∘Φ_j from step 1), for a single chart.

1. Φ is injective on Ω (if Φ(w) = Φ(w′) then c|w − w′| ≤ 0) and continuous on Ω (Lipschitz on Ω).
2. (Borel preimages.) For every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^P, Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B) is Borel: the map Φ̃ := Ω.piecewise Φ 0 (Φ on Ω, 0 off Ω) is Borel measurable (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise, Φ continuous on the measurable set Ω, the constant continuous on Ωᶜ), and Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B) = Ω ∩ Φ̃⁻¹(B).
3. (First conclusion.) Choose a Borel B ⊆ A with Hⁿ(A ∖ B) = 0 (NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq). Then D = (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B)) ∪ (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A ∖ B)); the first set is Borel by step 2 and the second is Lⁿ-null by the sibling lemma chart_preimage_null (with Z := A ∖ B). Hence D is Lⁿ-null-measurable.
4. (Second conclusion.) Choose a measurable g′ with g = g′ Hⁿ⌞A-a.e. Since A is null-measurable, Hⁿ⌞A(E) = Hⁿ(E ∩ A) for every E (Measure.restrict_apply₀'), so Z′ := {x : g(x) ≠ g′(x)} ∩ A is Hⁿ-null, and by chart_preimage_null Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z′)) = 0. For w ∈ D outside Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z′) we have Φ(w) ∈ A and g(Φ(w)) = g′(Φ(w)). Since Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. w lies in D (D null-measurable, ae_restrict_mem₀) and outside the null set Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z′) (ae_restrict_of_ae), g∘Φ = g′∘Φ Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. Moreover Φ is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞Ω (ContinuousOn.aemeasurable), hence for Lⁿ⌞D (D ⊆ Ω), so g′∘Φ is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞D (Measurable.comp_aemeasurable) and so is g∘Φ (AEMeasurable.congr).
5. (Area formula for Φ on D.) Φ is Lipschitz on Ω, hence locally Lipschitz on Ω (at each point use the neighbourhood Ω itself, self_mem_nhdsWithin). Apply the sibling lemma local_lipschitz_area with Q := P, the open set Ω, D ⊆ Ω (null-measurable by step 3), u := Φ and weight w ↦ g(Φ(w)) (a.e.-measurable by step 4): ∫_D g(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dLⁿ(w) = ∫_{ℝ^P} N dHⁿ with N(y) := Σ_{w ∈ D, Φ(w) = y} g(Φ(w)).
6. (Fibres.) N = 1_A·g pointwise. If y ∈ A, then y = Φ(w₀) for some w₀ ∈ Ω (A ⊆ Φ(Ω)); w₀ ∈ D and, by injectivity of Φ on Ω, the fibre {w ∈ D : Φ(w) = y} is exactly {w₀}, so N(y) = g(Φ(w₀)) = g(y) (tsum_eq_single). If y ∉ A, no w ∈ D satisfies Φ(w) = y because Φ(w) ∈ A for w ∈ D; the fibre is empty and N(y) = 0.
7. (Third conclusion.) ∫ N dHⁿ = ∫ 1_A·g dHⁿ = ∫_A g dHⁿ (lintegral_indicator₀, A null-measurable). With step 5, ∫_A g dHⁿ = ∫_D g(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dLⁿ(w). ∎
proof_key_steps: Φ is injective and continuous on Ω; Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Borel) is Borel (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise).
D = Borel part ∪ preimage of an Hⁿ-null set, null by chart_preimage_null: D is Lⁿ-null-measurable.
g∘Φ = g′∘Φ a.e. on D (g′ measurable) using chart_preimage_null on {g ≠ g′} ∩ A: a.e.-measurability.
local_lipschitz_area for u := Φ, weight g∘Φ on D ⊆ Ω.
By injectivity the fibre sum equals the indicator 1_A g; lintegral_indicator₀ gives ∫_A g dHⁿ.

subproblems.title: Jacobian identity ‖L_#ξ‖·J(A) = J(L∘A) for frames of the tangent plane
subproblems.statement: Assume (S1) ‖simpleNVector v‖² = det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} for all P, n and all v : Fin n → ℝ^P, and (S2) simpleNVector(i ↦ Σ_j B_ij τ_j) = det(B)·simpleNVector τ for all P, n, all real n×n matrices B and all τ : Fin n → ℝ^P (this conjunction is verbatim the frozen type of the already-reserved theorem lpf_simple_nvector_algebra; it is taken as a hypothesis so that this lemma is provable independently and the parent discharges it with Submission.lpf_simple_nvector_algebra). Then for all P, Q, n, every continuous linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, every orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with A(v) ∈ span{τ_1, …, τ_n} for all v, every n-vector ξ with ξ = simpleNVector τ or ξ = −simpleNVector τ, and every continuous linear L : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q: ‖L_#ξ‖·√det(⟨A e_i, A e_j⟩) = √det(⟨L A e_i, L A e_j⟩), where L_# = nVectorPushforward n L and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ((∀ (P n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Eucl P), ‖simpleNVector v‖ ^ 2 = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)).det) ∧ ∀ (P n : ℕ) (B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P), simpleNVector (fun i => ∑ j, B i j • τ j) = B.det • simpleNVector τ) → ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (A : Eucl n →L[ℝ] Eucl P) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P) (ξ : NVector (Eucl P) n) (L : Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (∀ v, A v ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (range τ)) → (ξ = simpleNVector τ ∨ ξ = -simpleNVector τ) → ‖nVectorPushforward n L ξ‖ * Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (A (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (A (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det = Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (L (A (EuclideanSpace.single i 1))) (L (A (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)))).det
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure); Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i : Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ. For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, JT := √det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Gram-determinant Jacobian); for a map φ, Jφ(w) := J(fderiv ℝ φ w). For B ⊆ X, a map f and a weight h ≥ 0, the fibre sum is N_B(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B, f(x) = y} h(x), the unordered sum in [0,∞] (∑' over the subtype {x // x ∈ B ∧ f x = y}). c-antilipschitz on Ω means c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is the linear algebra of step 3 of the parent proof (simpleNVector(A_w e) = det(B)·simpleNVector τ = ±det(B)·ξ(x), push forward by L(x)_#, take norms), stated for one linear map. The hypotheses (S1), (S2) are the two parts of the antecedent.

1. (Coefficients.) Put a_i := A e_i. Since a_i ∈ span(range τ), a_i = Σ_k c_k τ_k for some c (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun). Taking the inner product with τ_k and using orthonormality (⟨τ_k, τ_k⟩ = |τ_k|² = 1 and ⟨τ_k, τ_j⟩ = 0 for j ≠ k) gives c_k = ⟨τ_k, a_i⟩. Define the real n×n matrix B_ik := ⟨τ_k, a_i⟩; thus a_i = Σ_k B_ik τ_k for every i.
2. (Change of frame.) By (S2) applied to B and τ: simpleNVector a = det(B)·simpleNVector τ.
3. (Pushforward.) nVectorPushforward n L w = w ∘ covectorPullback n L is linear in w; in particular L_#(c·w) = c·L_#w and L_#(−w) = −L_#w (both hold by extensionality, definitionally). By nVectorPushforward_simple, L_#(simpleNVector a) = simpleNVector(L∘a). Hence, by step 2, simpleNVector(i ↦ L a_i) = det(B)·L_#(simpleNVector τ).
4. Since ξ = ±simpleNVector τ, L_#ξ = ±L_#(simpleNVector τ), so ‖L_#ξ‖ = ‖L_#(simpleNVector τ)‖ (norm_neg).
5. (Gram roots.) For any R and any family v : Fin n → ℝ^R, (S1) gives det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩) = ‖simpleNVector v‖², hence √det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩) = ‖simpleNVector v‖ (Real.sqrt_sq, norm ≥ 0).
6. (Unit frame.) τ orthonormal means ⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩ = δ_ij (orthonormal_iff_ite), so the Gram matrix of τ is the identity, with determinant 1; by (S1) ‖simpleNVector τ‖² = 1, so ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1.
7. (Scalars.) For c ∈ ℝ and an n-vector w, ‖c·w‖ = |c|·‖w‖ (operator norm; in Lean, if instance search does not provide NormSMulClass ℝ on NVector, prove ≤ by ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_smul_le and ≥ for c ≠ 0 by applying the same bound to c⁻¹·(c·w)).
8. (Conclusion.) Left side = ‖L_#ξ‖·‖simpleNVector a‖ (step 5 with R = P) = ‖L_#ξ‖·|det B|·‖simpleNVector τ‖ (steps 2, 7) = ‖L_#ξ‖·|det B| (step 6). Right side = ‖simpleNVector(i ↦ L a_i)‖ (step 5 with R = Q) = |det B|·‖L_#(simpleNVector τ)‖ (steps 3, 7) = |det B|·‖L_#ξ‖ (step 4). The two sides agree. (For n = 0 everything is uniform: B is the empty matrix, det B = 1.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Expand A e_i = Σ_k B_ik τ_k with B_ik = ⟨τ_k, A e_i⟩ (orthonormality).
(S2): simpleNVector(A e) = det B · simpleNVector τ; push forward by L (nVectorPushforward_simple, linearity in w).
‖L_#ξ‖ = ‖L_#(simpleNVector τ)‖ since ξ = ±simpleNVector τ.
(S1): √det Gram(v) = ‖simpleNVector v‖, and ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1 for orthonormal τ.
‖c·w‖ = |c|‖w‖; both sides equal |det B|·‖L_#ξ‖.

subproblems.title: A.e. Jacobian identity on a C¹ antilipschitz chart of a rectifiable triple
subproblems.statement: Assume (S1) ‖simpleNVector v‖² = det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} for all P, n and all v : Fin n → ℝ^P, and (S2) simpleNVector(i ↦ Σ_j B_ij τ_j) = det(B)·simpleNVector τ for all P, n, all real n×n matrices B and all τ : Fin n → ℝ^P (this conjunction is verbatim the frozen type of the already-reserved theorem lpf_simple_nvector_algebra; it is taken as a hypothesis so that this lemma is provable independently and the parent discharges it with Submission.lpf_simple_nvector_algebra). Let P, Q, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q, L : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q), Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P C¹ and c-antilipschitz on Ω for some c > 0, and suppose that for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M), range DΦ(w) is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at Φ(w) and f∘Φ has Fréchet derivative L(Φ(w))∘DΦ(w) at w. Then for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M): ‖L(Φ(w))_#ξ(Φ(w))‖ₑ·JΦ(w) = J(f∘Φ)(w) in [0,∞], where JΦ(w) = √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩) and J(f∘Φ)(w) = √det(⟨D(f∘Φ)(w)e_i, D(f∘Φ)(w)e_j⟩) (both embedded by ENNReal.ofReal).
subproblems.lean_statement: ((∀ (P n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Eucl P), ‖simpleNVector v‖ ^ 2 = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)).det) ∧ ∀ (P n : ℕ) (B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P), simpleNVector (fun i => ∑ j, B i j • τ j) = B.det • simpleNVector τ) → ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q) (L : Eucl P → (Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q)) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)), IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → (∀ᵐ w ∂((volume : Measure (Eucl n)).restrict (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' M)), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ (Φ w) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w).toLinearMap) ∧ HasFDerivAt (f ∘ Φ) ((L (Φ w)).comp (fderiv ℝ Φ w)) w) → ∀ᵐ w ∂((volume : Measure (Eucl n)).restrict (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' M)), ‖nVectorPushforward n (L (Φ w)) (ξ (Φ w))‖ₑ * ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det) = ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure); Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i : Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ. For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, JT := √det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Gram-determinant Jacobian); for a map φ, Jφ(w) := J(fderiv ℝ φ w). For B ⊆ X, a map f and a weight h ≥ 0, the fibre sum is N_B(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B, f(x) = y} h(x), the unordered sum in [0,∞] (∑' over the subtype {x // x ∈ B ∧ f x = y}). c-antilipschitz on Ω means c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is steps 2–3 of the parent proof (good parameters and the Jacobian identity J(x)·JΦ_j(w) = Ju_j(w)) for one chart; the chain-rule hypothesis is exactly the conclusion of the frozen theorem lpf_chart_chain_rule, which the parent supplies.

1. (S is null-measurable.) S := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M). M is Hⁿ-null-measurable (IsRectifiableTriple.nullMeasurableSet); choose a Borel B ⊆ M with Hⁿ(M ∖ B) = 0. Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B) is Borel (Φ is continuous, being C¹, and Ω is open), and Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M ∖ B) is Lⁿ-null by the sibling lemma chart_preimage_null. S is their union, hence Lⁿ-null-measurable.
2. (Transfer of orients.) Let G be the set of x ∈ ℝ^P for which there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P such that span(range τ) is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x and ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ. The field orients of IsRectifiableTriple says Hⁿ⌞M(Gᶜ) = 0 (ae_iff); as M is null-measurable, Hⁿ⌞M(Gᶜ) = Hⁿ(Gᶜ ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_apply₀'), so Hⁿ(Gᶜ ∩ M) = 0. By chart_preimage_null, Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Gᶜ ∩ M)) = 0. Hence for Lⁿ-a.e. w, w ∈ S implies Φ(w) ∈ G. Since Lⁿ⌞S ≪ Lⁿ (ae_restrict_of_ae) and Lⁿ⌞S-a.e. w lies in S (ae_restrict_mem₀, step 1), Φ(w) ∈ G for Lⁿ⌞S-a.e. w.
3. (Good parameters.) Intersecting the a.e. sets of the hypothesis, of step 2 and of ae_restrict_mem₀: for Lⁿ⌞S-a.e. w we have w ∈ S, Φ(w) ∈ G, (i) HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ (Φ w) (range DΦ(w)) and (ii) HasFDerivAt (f∘Φ) (L(Φ w)∘DΦ(w)) w. Fix such a w and put x := Φ(w).
4. (Uniqueness of the tangent plane.) x ∈ M, so θ(x) > 0 (IsRectifiableTriple.pos) and θ(x) ≠ 0. Let τ witness x ∈ G. By uniqueness of weighted approximate tangent spaces at points of nonzero multiplicity (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), range DΦ(w) = span(range τ); in particular DΦ(w)v ∈ span(range τ) for every v (LinearMap.mem_range_self).
5. (Linear algebra.) Apply the sibling lemma jacobian_identity (passing it the assumed (S1) ∧ (S2)) with A := DΦ(w), τ, ξ := ξ(x) and L := L(x): ‖L(x)_#ξ(x)‖·JΦ(w) = √det(⟨L(x)DΦ(w)e_i, L(x)DΦ(w)e_j⟩).
6. (Chain rule.) By (ii), fderiv ℝ (f∘Φ) w = L(x)∘DΦ(w) (HasFDerivAt.fderiv), and (L(x)∘DΦ(w))e_i = L(x)(DΦ(w)e_i) (ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply); so the right side of step 5 is J(f∘Φ)(w).
7. (Passing to [0,∞].) ‖v‖ₑ = ofReal ‖v‖ (ofReal_norm) and ofReal(a)·ofReal(b) = ofReal(a·b) for a ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul); hence ‖L(x)_#ξ(x)‖ₑ·ofReal(JΦ(w)) = ofReal(‖L(x)_#ξ(x)‖·JΦ(w)) = ofReal(J(f∘Φ)(w)). This holds for Lⁿ⌞S-a.e. w. ∎
proof_key_steps: Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) is Lⁿ-null-measurable (Borel part plus chart_preimage_null).
orients holds at Φ(w) for a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) (Hⁿ-null exceptional set pulled back by chart_preimage_null).
θ(Φ w) > 0 and HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique give range DΦ(w) = span τ.
jacobian_identity with A = DΦ(w), L = L(Φ w); HasFDerivAt.fderiv identifies D(f∘Φ)(w) = L(Φ w)∘DΦ(w).
Convert to [0,∞] with ofReal_norm and ENNReal.ofReal_mul.

subproblems.title: Area formula on one chart piece from the a.e. Jacobian identity
subproblems.statement: Let P, Q, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q locally Lipschitz on U, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz on Ω and c-antilipschitz on Ω for some c > 0, J, h : ℝ^P → [0,∞], and A ⊆ ℝ^P with A ⊆ U, A ⊆ Φ(Ω), A Hⁿ-null-measurable, h and J a.e.-measurable for Hⁿ⌞A. Write JΦ(w) := √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩)_{i,j} and J(f∘Φ)(w) := √det(⟨D(f∘Φ)(w)e_i, D(f∘Φ)(w)e_j⟩)_{i,j}, where D = fderiv ℝ and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Suppose J(Φ(w))·ofReal(JΦ(w)) = ofReal(J(f∘Φ)(w)) in [0,∞] for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A). Then N_A(y) := Σ_{x ∈ A, f(x) = y} h(x) is Hⁿ-a.e. measurable on ℝ^Q and ∫_A h·J dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝ^Q} N_A dHⁿ.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure); Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i : Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ. For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, JT := √det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Gram-determinant Jacobian); for a map φ, Jφ(w) := J(fderiv ℝ φ w). For B ⊆ X, a map f and a weight h ≥ 0, the fibre sum is N_B(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B, f(x) = y} h(x), the unordered sum in [0,∞] (∑' over the subtype {x // x ∈ B ∧ f x = y}). c-antilipschitz on Ω means c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is steps 4–5 of the parent proof for one chart piece A_j (∫_{A_j} hJ dHⁿ = ∫_{D_j} h(Φ_j w) J(Φ_j w) JΦ_j(w) dw = ∫_{D_j} h(Φ_j w) Ju_j(w) dw = ∫ N_{A_j} dHⁿ, with the bijection Φ_j : D_j → A_j), with the Jacobian J abstracted.

1. Let D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A). Φ is injective on Ω (c > 0: Φ(w) = Φ(w′) forces c|w − w′| ≤ 0) and continuous on Ω (Lipschitz).
2. (Source change of variables.) h·J is a.e.-measurable for Hⁿ⌞A (product of a.e.-measurable functions, AEMeasurable.mul). The sibling lemma chart_change_of_variables with g := h·J gives: D is Lⁿ-null-measurable and ∫_A h·J dHⁿ = ∫_D h(Φ(w))·J(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dLⁿ(w). Applied with g := h it also gives that w ↦ h(Φ(w)) is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞D.
3. (Jacobian substitution.) By hypothesis, for Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. w, h(Φ(w))·J(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) = h(Φ(w))·J(f∘Φ)(w) (associativity of multiplication). Hence ∫_A h·J dHⁿ = ∫_D h(Φ(w))·J(f∘Φ)(w) dLⁿ(w) (lintegral_congr_ae).
4. (Open domain for f∘Φ.) Ω′ := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(U) is open (ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage: Φ continuous on the open Ω, U open), and D ⊆ Ω′ because A ⊆ U.
5. (f∘Φ is locally Lipschitz on Ω′.) Let w ∈ Ω′, so Φ(w) ∈ U. Local Lipschitzness of f on U gives K′ and t ∈ 𝓝[U] Φ(w) with f K′-Lipschitz on t. Φ is continuous within Ω′ at w and maps Ω′ into U, so Φ tends to 𝓝[U] Φ(w) along 𝓝[Ω′] w (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff), whence Ω′ ∩ Φ⁻¹(t) ∈ 𝓝[Ω′] w. On this set Φ is K-Lipschitz (it lies in Ω) with values in t, so f∘Φ is K′K-Lipschitz there (LipschitzOnWith.comp).
6. (Area formula for f∘Φ.) Apply the sibling lemma local_lipschitz_area to Ω′, D ⊆ Ω′ (null-measurable by step 2), u := f∘Φ and the weight w ↦ h(Φ(w)) (a.e.-measurable by step 2): Ñ(y) := Σ_{w ∈ D, f(Φ(w)) = y} h(Φ(w)) is Hⁿ-a.e. measurable and ∫_D h(Φ(w))·J(f∘Φ)(w) dLⁿ(w) = ∫ Ñ dHⁿ.
7. (Fibre transport.) For each y, w ↦ Φ(w) is a bijection from {w : w ∈ D, f(Φ(w)) = y} onto {x : x ∈ A, f(x) = y}: it is well defined (Φ(w) ∈ A), injective (Φ injective on Ω), and surjective (x ∈ A ⊆ Φ(Ω) gives w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = x; then w ∈ D and f(Φ(w)) = y). Reindexing the unordered sum along it (Equiv.ofBijective, Equiv.tsum_eq) gives Ñ(y) = N_A(y) for every y.
8. (Conclusions.) N_A = Ñ is Hⁿ-a.e. measurable by step 6, and by steps 3, 6, 7: ∫_A h·J dHⁿ = ∫_D h(Φ(w))·J(f∘Φ)(w) dLⁿ(w) = ∫ Ñ dHⁿ = ∫ N_A dHⁿ. ∎

Substitute J(Φ w)·JΦ(w) = J(f∘Φ)(w) a.e. on D.
f∘Φ is locally Lipschitz on the open set Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(U) ⊇ D.

Φ is a bijection between the D-fibres of f∘Φ and the A-fibres of f; reindex the sums.

subproblems.title: A.e.-measurability of x ↦ ‖L(x)_#ξ(x)‖ₑ
subproblems.statement: For all P, Q, n ∈ ℕ, every measure μ on ℝ^P, and all L : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) and ξ : ℝ^P → NVector(ℝ^P, n) that are μ-a.e. strongly measurable, the function x ↦ ‖nVectorPushforward n (L x) (ξ x)‖ₑ is μ-a.e. measurable.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (L : Eucl P → (Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q)) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), AEStronglyMeasurable L μ → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → AEMeasurable (fun x => ‖nVectorPushforward n (L x) (ξ x)‖ₑ) μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k); NVector(ℝ^k, n) is the space of n-vectors (continuous linear functionals on n-covectors) with the operator norm; L_# = nVectorPushforward n L.

This is the measurability claim of step 4 of the parent proof (hJ is a.e.-measurable since h, L and ξ are and (A, w) ↦ ‖A_#w‖ is continuous).

1. (Joint continuity.) The map Π : L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) × NVector(ℝ^P, n) → NVector(ℝ^Q, n), Π(T, w) := nVectorPushforward n T w = w ∘ covectorPullback n T, is continuous: T ↦ covectorPullback n T = ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM T is continuous (ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM, composed with continuous_fst), and composition of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous (Continuous.clm_comp with continuous_snd).
2. (Composition.) x ↦ (L(x), ξ(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk), hence so is x ↦ Π(L(x), ξ(x)) (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable). The norm is continuous, so (T, w) ↦ ‖Π(T, w)‖ is continuous (Continuous.norm; if instance unification between ContinuousLinearMap.hasOpNorm and SeminormedAddGroup.toNorm needs help, state the codomain type explicitly, e.g. Continuous.norm (E := NVector (Eucl Q) n)), and x ↦ ‖L(x)_#ξ(x)‖ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, hence μ-a.e. measurable; therefore x ↦ ENNReal.ofReal ‖L(x)_#ξ(x)‖ is μ-a.e. measurable (AEMeasurable.ennreal_ofReal).
3. (Extended norm.) For every v, ‖v‖ₑ = ENNReal.ofReal ‖v‖ (ofReal_norm), so x ↦ ‖L(x)_#ξ(x)‖ₑ equals the function of step 2 pointwise and is μ-a.e. measurable (AEMeasurable.congr with the pointwise identity). ∎
proof_key_steps: (T, w) ↦ w ∘ covectorPullback n T is jointly continuous (continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM, Continuous.clm_comp).
Compose with the a.e. strongly measurable pair (L, ξ) and the continuous norm.
‖v‖ₑ = ofReal ‖v‖ gives a.e.-measurability of the extended norm.
